text:
Liam: Heads up — saw a quality regression on mixtral-8b that lines up with yesterday's runtime change (attention kernel swap + RoPE scaling toggle). Pasting quick repro and profiler snippets.\
Anika: ugh, where do you see it? production or canary?
Liam: Canary first. Failed our scoring eval: hallucination rate up ~3.1% on commonsense prompt set after the kernel swap. Perf looks fine (throughput +8%) but outputs diverge.
Sophia: Can you paste the eval example?
Liam: Sure — short sample from eval harness:
```
# prompt
Q: Why did the vase break when dropped?
A:
# baseline
Because it hit the floor and shattered due to impact, producing shards.
# after-change
Because the glass wanted to be free. It escaped and broke into tiny feelings.
```
Anika: lol that's bad. matches the regression class we saw with rope scaling mismatches before. Any kernel logs?
Liam: Profiling traces show attention path changed to our new fwd_sparse kernel for short seqs; kv-cache checksum shows a mismatch on reuse buckets for heads 8-11. Profiler snippet:
```
ATTN_KERNEL: fwd_sparse (selected)
LATENCY: p50 12ms, p99 95ms
KV_CACHE_HITS: 0.87
KV_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH: 0.0022
BATCH_SIZES_SAMPLE: [1,4,8]
```
Matt: kv checksum mismatch is worrying — could be off-by-one in head-splitting or RoPE scaling coefficients not applied consistently across kernels. Did you test with quant toggles?
Liam: Yes. The regression only triggers when runtime.quantized_attention=true AND rope_scale=auto. With quant=false the outputs match baseline.
Sophia: So two axes interacting: kernel swap picks quantized path, and rope_scale=auto picks a per-head scale that our new kernel applies slightly differently. If float path and quant false then we fallback to dense kernel and it's fine.
Anika: Can we reproduce locally with unit test? Small script that toggles kernels and compares logits/kv-checksum across steps.
Liam: I already wrote a mini repro. Will push gist in a sec. Protodiff shows per-head kv vectors off by ~1e-2 after 3 tokens when quantized kernel used.
PerfBot: Regression-alert: mixtral-8b eval_suite.hallucination increased by 3.1% at 2026-03-15T21:03:30Z. Linked: https://perf.redwood/reports/3456
Matt: My guess: quantized kernel uses int8 matmul with a different accumulation order; combined with RoPE scaling we get numeric drift that flips top logits for ambiguous completions. That explains hallucinations.
Sophia: Also check softmax numerics in that kernel — int accumulation can produce slightly different normalization leading to sampling divergence.
Anika: What's the mitigation plan? Patch kernel, or rollback?
Liam: I proposed a short-term rollback on canary: force kernel selection to 'dense-atten' for mixtral-8b when quantized. Flag: runtime.kernels.attn_forced=dense for that model. We'll run full eval and extended canary.
Matt: +1 rollback. Also open PR to add head-dim consistency asserts and KV checksum test in CI so this doesn't slip.
Sophia: Agreed. For longer term we need to align RoPE application code paths (quant vs float) and add unit tests with perturbed scales.
Anika: Who will coordinate rollback?
Liam: I'll submit the rollback patch and request DeployBot for a canary rollback. Assigning myself and Matt to follow up on the kernel fix.
DeployBot: @Liam, canary rollback job queued: job id cb-2026-1458. Will notify when done.
Liam: Thanks. After rollback we'll run the eval harness with the following matrix: models=[mixtral-8b, mixtral-8b-quant], ropescale=[auto, fixed-1.0], kernels=[dense, fwd_sparse], batching=[1,4,8]. Will post results.
Matt: Also add a small randomized prompt set to catch sampling instabilities early.
PerfBot: Canary rollback complete for mixtral-8b canary (cb-2026-1458). Post-rollback eval: hallucination delta now +0.1% (within noise).
Sophia: Nice — rollback looks clean. Liam/Matt please follow up with kernel PR and CI guards. I'll draft a postmortem note for eng-runtime so product and CS know about the brief regression.
Liam: Will do. PR draft: "fix(atten-kernel): align RoPE application and accumulation order in quantized path" — I'll link tests and repro.
Anika: Thanks all. Add an alert rule to flag kv checksum mismatch >0.001 in future. :thumbsup:
Liam: Good call. Creating alert ticket now.
